summary: API Gateway + upstream elevated 5xx (gradual error drift) traced to accept-queue saturation on select runtime hosts
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-10 00:20 UTC we observed a slow, persistent increase in 5xx responses for a subset of tenant traffic in prod-us-west. Impact: customer-facing errors (502/504) at 3-8% sustained with short spikes to ~18% on small bursts. Impacted customers included BrightMarket Labs (dedicated). Environment: prod-us-west, API gateway fronting multiple serving-runtime pools, prefetched KV caching enabled for affected workloads. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of concurrent streaming generate calls (concurrency 40-60) to tenant endpoint pinned to rw-llama-13b-v2. 2) Observe error rate slowly increase over 30-90 minutes, not an immediate spike. 3) When error rate climbs, confirmed that only a subset of runtime hosts also show increased process restarts and accept backlog growth. Observed behaviour: - API gateway logs show a rise in upstream: "connection reset by peer" and "upstream timed out" over hours. - Runtime hosts with issues show accept queue length growth (netstat backlog > 1024) and rapid fd table usage approaching ulimit. - Runtime process (worker) restarts seen in k8s events correlating with accept queue saturation rather than OOM. - Autoscaler did not immediately add capacity because node-level health checks remained green until the accept backlog crossed kernel thresholds. Expected behaviour: Stable error rate <0.1% for similar workload. Logs/metrics: - apigw logs sample: "[2026-03-10T01:42:13Z] upstream error: connection reset by peer (upstream: http://10.4.22.13:8080) request_id=..." - runtime host syslog: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" (host-10-4-22-13) - netstat excerpt: "tcp        0      0 10.4.22.13:8080       0.0.0.0:*               LISTEN      12345/process (backlog=2048)" - k8s events: "Backoff restarting failed container" Investigation hypothesis: The pattern is slow drift (not a sudden surge) which suggests a connection lifecycle misbehavior. Initial hypothesis: a change in container base image (rolling update two days prior) altered libuv/tcp keepalive handling -> accumulation of sockets in TIME_WAIT/half-open state and accept queue backlog growth. Secondary hypothesis: intermittent kernel-level conntrack pressure combined with a small regression in the edge-proxy causing uneven connection distribution (SO_REUSEPORT skew) leading to a subset of runtimes receiving disproportionate new connections and hitting fd limits. Workaround applied: 1) Increased accept backlog and ulimit for affected PODs via daemonset patch (temporary) and rolled a new edge-proxy config to enable shorter keepalive on upstreams. 2) Bumped autoscaler to be more aggressive for the tenant pool to move traffic to healthy hosts. Follow-up required: revert the base-image change or apply fix in runtime to avoid half-open socket retention, tune conntrack and iptables settings for short term, and add guardrails in autoscaler to detect accept-queue saturation.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 00:20 UTC - first small increase observed in edge dashboards. 00:45 UTC - SRE noticed accept backlog growth on three runtime nodes. 01:10 UTC - applied temporary backlog/ulimit increase; error rate dropped from 18% spike to 4%. 02:00 UTC - rolled edge-proxy keepalive timeout change; sustained error rate returned to baseline by 03:15 UTC. Findings: - Hosts that hit the state had 2.5x higher new connection counts compared to peers. - fd_table utilization was at 92% on problematic hosts; no OOMs. - Kernel conntrack metrics showed short bursts of table-full events leading to dropped packets. Evidence: logs and netstat excerpts uploaded to internal S3 (link posted in comments). Next steps: 1) Validate and merge runtime fix in PR #5941 to ensure sockets are closed promptly (owner: infra/serving). 2) Add accept-queue and fd watermark alert to SRE monitoring. 3) Add an autoscaler probe for accept-queue/backlog to prefer healthy hosts sooner. 4) Run a canary of base-image rollback vs runtime patch to confirm root cause.
resolution_notes: Temporary mitigation successful: increased backlog/ulimit and shorter upstream keepalive reduced error rate to baseline by 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC. Root cause under patch: regression in runtime socket handling combined with conntrack pressure and uneven load distribution from edge-proxy. Candidate permanent fixes: runtime patch (PR #5941) to close accept-side sockets earlier, edge-proxy change for more even distribution, and autoscaler change to detect backlog saturation. Action items: - Merge and deploy PR #5941, monitor for 48 hours. - Add monitoring alert for accept backlog > 1024 and fd_util > 85% to trigger autoscaler policy. - Schedule post-mortem and update runbook.
